modern.text: Through your servants you have taunted the Lord, and you have said: “With my many chariots I have ascended to the heights of the mountains, to the remote peaks of Lebanon. I have cut down its tallest cedars, the finest of its cypresses. I have reached its farthest outposts, the densest of its forests.

original.text: בְּיַ֣ד מַלְאָכֶיךָ֮ חֵרַ֣פְתָּ אֲדֹנָי֒ וַתֹּ֗אמֶר ברכב רִכְבִּ֛י אֲנִ֥י עָלִ֛יתִי מְר֥וֹם הָרִ֖ים יַרְכְּתֵ֣י לְבָנ֑וֹן וְאֶכְרֹ֞ת קוֹמַ֤ת אֲרָזָיו֙ מִבְח֣וֹר בְּרֹשָׁ֔יו וְאָב֨וֹאָה֙ מְל֣וֹן קִצֹּ֔ה יַ֖עַר כַּרְמִלּֽוֹ

verses.restored: I dug and drank foreign waters, and with soles of my feet dried all streams of besieged places.

familiar.text: I have digged and drunk strange waters, and with the sole of my feet have I dried up all the rivers of besieged places.

modern.text: I have dug wells and drunk foreign waters. With the soles of my feet I have dried up all the streams of Egypt.”

original.text: אֲנִ֣י קַ֔רְתִּי וְשָׁתִ֖יתִי מַ֣יִם זָרִ֑ים וְאַחְרִב֙ בְּכַף פְּעָמַ֔י כֹּ֖ל יְאֹרֵ֥י מָצֽוֹר

verses.restored: Have you not heard? From far ago I made it; from days of old I formed it. Now I brought it to pass, that you should make fortified cities into ruined heaps.

familiar.text: Hast thou not heard long ago how I have done it, and of ancient times that I have formed it? now have I brought it to pass, that thou shouldest be to lay waste fenced cities into ruinous heaps.

modern.text: Have you not heard? Long ago I ordained it; in days of old I planned it. Now I have brought it to pass, that you should crush fortified cities into piles of rubble.

original.text: הֲלֹֽא שָׁמַ֤עְתָּ לְמֵֽרָחוֹק֙ אֹתָ֣הּ עָשִׂ֔יתִי לְמִ֥ימֵי קֶ֖דֶם וִֽיצַרְתִּ֑יהָ עַתָּ֣ה הֲבֵיאתִ֗יהָ וּתְהִ֗י לַהְשׁ֛וֹת גַּלִּ֥ים נִצִּ֖ים עָרִ֥ים בְּצֻרֽוֹת

verses.restored: Their inhabitants were short of hand, shattered and ashamed; they became grass of field, green herb, grass of roofs, and scorched grain before standing.

familiar.text: Therefore their inhabitants were of small power, they were dismayed and confounded; they were as the grass of the field, and as the green herb, as the grass on the house tops, and as corn blasted before it be grown up.

modern.text: Therefore their inhabitants, devoid of power, are dismayed and ashamed. They are like plants in the field, tender green shoots, grass on the rooftops, scorched before it is grown.

original.text: וְיֹֽשְׁבֵיהֶן֙ קִצְרֵי יָ֔ד חַ֖תּוּ וַיֵּבֹ֑שׁוּ הָי֞וּ עֵ֤שֶׂב שָׂדֶה֙ וִ֣ירַק דֶּ֔שֶׁא חֲצִ֣יר גַּגּ֔וֹת וּשְׁדֵפָ֖ה לִפְנֵ֥י קָמָֽה

verses.restored: But your sitting, going out, coming in, and raging against me I know.

familiar.text: But I know thy abode, and thy going out, and thy coming in, and thy rage against me.

modern.text: But I know your sitting down, your going out and coming in, and your raging against Me.

original.text: וְשִׁבְתְּךָ֛ וְצֵאתְךָ֥ וּבֹאֲךָ֖ יָדָ֑עְתִּי וְאֵ֖ת הִֽתְרַגֶּזְךָ֥ אֵלָֽי

verses.restored: Because your raging against me and arrogance rose into my ears, I will put my hook in your nose and bridle in your lips and turn you back by way you came.

familiar.text: Because thy rage against me and thy tumult is come up into mine ears, therefore I will put my hook in thy nose, and my bridle in thy lips, and I will turn thee back by the way by which thou camest.

modern.text: Because your rage and arrogance against Me have reached My ears, I will put My hook in your nose and My bit in your mouth; I will send you back the way you came.’

original.text: יַ֚עַן הִתְרַגֶּזְךָ֣ אֵלַ֔י וְשַׁאֲנַנְךָ֖ עָלָ֣ה בְאָזְנָ֑י וְשַׂמְתִּ֨י חַחִ֜י בְּאַפֶּ֗ךָ וּמִתְגִּי֙ בִּשְׂפָתֶ֔יךָ וַהֲשִׁ֣בֹתִ֔יךָ בַּדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֲשֶׁר בָּ֥אתָ בָּֽהּ

verses.restored: This shall be sign for you: eat this year what grows of itself, second year what springs from it, and in third year sow, reap, plant vineyards, and eat their fruit.

familiar.text: And this shall be a sign unto thee, Ye shall eat this year such things as grow of themselves, and in the second year that which springeth of the same; and in the third year sow ye, and reap, and plant vineyards, and eat the fruits thereof.

modern.text: And this will be a sign to you, O Hezekiah: This year you will eat what grows on its own, and in the second year what springs from the same. But in the third year you will sow and reap; you will plant vineyards and eat their fruit.

original.text: וְזֶה לְּךָ֣ הָא֔וֹת אָכ֤וֹל הַשָּׁנָה֙ סָפִ֔יחַ וּבַשָּׁנָ֥ה הַשֵּׁנִ֖ית סָחִ֑ישׁ וּבַשָּׁנָ֣ה הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֗ית זִרְע֧וּ וְקִצְר֛וּ וְנִטְע֥וּ כְרָמִ֖ים וְאִכְל֥וּ פִרְיָֽם

verses.restored: Surviving remnant of house of Judah shall again take root downward and bear fruit upward.

familiar.text: And the remnant that is escaped of the house of Judah shall yet again take root downward, and bear fruit upward.

modern.text: And the surviving remnant of the house of Judah will again take root below and bear fruit above.

original.text: וְיָ֨סְפָ֜ה פְּלֵיטַ֧ת בֵּית יְהוּדָ֛ה הַנִּשְׁאָרָ֖ה שֹׁ֣רֶשׁ לְמָ֑טָּה וְעָשָׂ֥ה פְרִ֖י לְמָֽעְלָה

verses.restored: For from Jerusalem a remnant shall go out, and survivors from Mount Zion. Zeal of YHWH of hosts shall do this.

familiar.text: For out of Jerusalem shall go forth a remnant, and they that escape out of mount Zion: the zeal of the LORD of hosts shall do this.

modern.text: For a remnant will go forth from Jerusalem, and survivors from Mount Zion. The zeal of the LORD of Hosts will accomplish this.

original.text: כִּ֤י מִירוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ תֵּצֵ֣א שְׁאֵרִ֔ית וּפְלֵיטָ֖ה מֵהַ֣ר צִיּ֑וֹן קִנְאַ֛ת יְהוָ֥ה תַּֽעֲשֶׂה זֹּֽאת

verses.restored: Therefore thus says YHWH concerning king of Assyria: He shall not come into this city, shoot an arrow there, come before it with shield, or pour up siege ramp against it.

familiar.text: Therefore thus saith the LORD concerning the king of Assyria, He shall not come into this city, nor shoot an arrow there, nor come before it with shield, nor cast a bank against it.

modern.text: So this is what the LORD says about the king of Assyria: ‘He will not enter this city or shoot an arrow into it. He will not come before it with a shield or build up a siege ramp against it.

original.text: לָכֵ֗ן כֹּֽה אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֶל מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר לֹ֤א יָבֹא֙ אֶל הָעִ֣יר הַזֹּ֔את וְלֹֽא יוֹרֶ֥ה שָׁ֖ם חֵ֑ץ וְלֹֽא יְקַדְּמֶ֣נָּה מָגֵ֔ן וְלֹֽא יִשְׁפֹּ֥ךְ עָלֶ֖יהָ סֹלְלָֽה

verses.restored: By way he came, by it he shall return, and to this city he shall not come, says YHWH.

familiar.text: By the way that he came, by the same shall he return, and shall not come into this city, saith the LORD.

modern.text: He will go back the way he came, and he will not enter this city,’ declares the LORD.

original.text: בַּדֶּ֥רֶךְ אֲשֶׁר יָבֹ֖א בָּ֣הּ יָשׁ֑וּב וְאֶל הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֛את לֹ֥א יָבֹ֖א נְאֻם יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: I will shield this city to save it, for my sake and for sake of David my servant.

familiar.text: For I will defend this city, to save it, for mine own sake, and for my servant David’s sake.

modern.text: ‘I will defend this city and save it for My own sake and for the sake of My servant David.’” Jerusalem Delivered from the Assyrians (2 Chronicles 32:20–23; Isaiah 37:36–38)

original.text: וְגַנּוֹתִ֛י אֶל הָעִ֥יר הַזֹּ֖את לְהֽוֹשִׁיעָ֑הּ לְמַֽעֲנִ֔י וּלְמַ֖עַן דָּוִ֥ד עַבְדִּֽי

verses.restored: That night messenger of YHWH went out and struck in camp of Assyria one hundred eighty-five thousand. They rose early in morning, and look, all of them were dead bodies.

familiar.text: And it came to pass that night, that the angel of the LORD went out, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians an hundred fourscore and five thousand: and when they arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses.

modern.text: And that very night the angel of the LORD went out and struck down 185,000 men in the camp of the Assyrians. When the people got up the next morning, there were all the dead bodies!

original.text: וַיְהִי֮ בַּלַּ֣יְלָה הַהוּא֒ וַיֵּצֵ֣א מַלְאַ֣ךְ יְהוָ֗ה וַיַּךְ֙ בְּמַחֲנֵ֣ה אַשּׁ֔וּר מֵאָ֛ה שְׁמוֹנִ֥ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֖ה אָ֑לֶף וַיַּשְׁכִּ֣ימוּ בַבֹּ֔קֶר וְהִנֵּ֥ה כֻלָּ֖ם פְּגָרִ֥ים מֵתִֽים

verses.restored: Sennacherib king of Assyria departed, went, returned, and lived at Nineveh.

familiar.text: So Sennacherib king of Assyria departed, and went and returned, and dwelt at Nineveh.

modern.text: So Sennacherib king of Assyria broke camp and withdrew. He returned to Nineveh and stayed there.

original.text: וַיִּסַּ֣ע וַיֵּ֔לֶךְ וַיָּ֖שָׁב סַנְחֵרִ֣יב מֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁ֑וּר וַיֵּ֖שֶׁב בְּנִֽינְוֵֽה

verses.restored: As he bowed in house of Nisroch his god, Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons struck him with sword and escaped to land of Ararat. Esarhaddon his son became king in his place.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, as he was worshipping in the house of Nisroch his god, that Adrammelech and Sharezer his sons smote him with the sword: and they escaped into the land of Armenia. And Esarhaddon his son reigned in his stead.

modern.text: One day, while he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch, his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer put him to the sword and escaped to the land of Ararat. And his son Esar-haddon reigned in his place.

original.text: וַיְהִי֩ ה֨וּא מִֽשְׁתַּחֲוֶ֜ה בֵּ֣ית נִסְרֹ֣ךְ אֱלֹהָ֗יו וְֽאַדְרַמֶּ֨לֶךְ וְשַׂרְאֶ֤צֶר הִכֻּ֣הוּ בַחֶ֔רֶב וְהֵ֥מָּה נִמְלְט֖וּ אֶ֣רֶץ אֲרָרָ֑ט וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אֵֽסַר חַדֹּ֥ן בְּנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו

translation_notes: Hezekiah's torn clothes and sackcloth are crisis rituals, not signs that fear or grief is weak faith.
The birth metaphor describes a community at the point of delivery without strength. It must not shame laboring people, pregnancy complications, infertility, pregnancy loss, or medical intervention.
Hezekiah spreads the threatening letter before YHWH; prayer here brings propaganda into honest scrutiny rather than denying military reality.
The prayer polemic calls other gods human-made. It belongs to Israelite monotheistic theology and must not authorize destruction, ridicule, or persecution of living religious communities.
Assyria boasts of deforestation, water control, siege, and ruined cities. Imperial domination includes ecological extraction and destruction.
The hook-in-nose and bridle imagery reflects Assyrian practices of humiliating captives. It is a reversal of imperial violence, not permission for torture.
Agricultural recovery unfolds across three years. Survival after siege includes food systems, planting, time, labor, and land restoration—not an instant return to normal.
Verse 35 reports mass death of 185,000 Assyrians through Divine agency. This is morally dangerous sacred-war material and must not be celebrated, reenacted, or used to pray for mass killing.
Assyrian soldiers are human beings, many under command. Jerusalem's deliverance does not make their corpses spiritually delightful.
Sennacherib is later assassinated by sons in a temple. Patricide and political assassination remain violence; another religion's sanctuary must not be mocked.
Kings/Isaiah/Chronicles and Assyrian sources require historical and source-witness audit regarding the campaign, withdrawal, chronology, and casualty tradition.
safety_note: Do not turn Jerusalem's rescue into joy over 185,000 dead people, justify holy war, mock other religions, or romanticize assassination. Center fear, prayer, remnant survival, agricultural recovery, civilians under siege, conscripted soldiers, and the refusal of empire's claim to be morally unstoppable.
